judgments.reasoning_cat1: "in waiting" is a scrivener's slip for "in writing", and "or in such form as may be acceptable to the Company" leaves the required form of notice entirely open, though little turns on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision prescribes a notice mechanic that this contradicts; the forfeiture and termination clauses operate without notice requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, standard savings clause preserving the Company's other remedies after forfeiture; nothing in it invites two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Sections 2.b, 2.c and 14, which impose the forfeitures it preserves rights alongside.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Giving the Company "sole and absolute discretion" over any "interpretation, construction or application" that is "final, binding and conclusive" is a one-sided grant whose reach — whether it ousts judicial review or is limited by good faith — is precisely the kind of thing parties fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against Section 9's Texas governing-law clause and the closing acknowledgment that the Company "may exercise legal means to enforce" the Agreement, and if read literally it would make the Payment promise in Section 1 illusory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause binds only "each successor and assign of the Company" and says nothing about the employee's side, a one-sided drafting that leaves its scope arguable but is a common formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble defines the employee to include "your heirs and successors" and Sections 2.a and 3 contemplate payment to an estate or by will, so the omission here is a small mismatch with the front of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: OCR noise aside ("Lay", "lava"), the choice of Texas law without renvoi is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Agreement selects a different law or forum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional unfunded/no-trust clause; the dropped noun in "a benefit under this" is obvious from context and changes nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section 1's contractual payment promise and with Section 11's exclusion of the Payment from benefit plans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain exclusion of the Payment from pension, retirement, profit-sharing or welfare plan calculations and from base pay; the enumerated list is closed and workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably with Section 10 (unfunded, no plan status) and with the Payment's one-off character under Section 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The badly degraded text turns on "benefits or rights to which you are otherwise entitled ... immediately prior to" the amendment — whether a contingent, unvested Payment is such a right is genuinely contestable, and the sentence trails off after "statute or rules and regulations".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: An unlimited right to terminate the Agreement is hard to reconcile with the Term clause's fixed Retention Period and with Sections 1 and 2.a, and its no-diminution proviso pulls against the forfeiture rules in 2.b, 2.c and 14.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate severability clause; the garbling ("filly severable", "ag if") does not obscure the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It operates on the rest of the instrument generically and conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "threaten to disclose" is vague and the permitted-disclosure list (spouse, accountant, tax advisor, lawyer, or as required by law) is a closed enumeration whose reach against, say, a regulator or a court filing is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its "Notwithstanding any other provision" total forfeiture collides with Section 12's promise that nothing shall diminish rights without consent and with the graduated proration/forfeiture scheme in Section 2, and it also sits uneasily with Section 6's preservation of other remedies.
